profiles.meeting_scenario: A Jakarta law firm's environmental practice is preparing a coordinated client advisory and supporting annex for an international foundation that plans to brief Indonesian policymakers on legal gaps in managing marine plastic debris pollution. The advisory must explain the current Indonesian legal framework, the status of the 70% by 2025 reduction effort, and examples of how marine plastic debris rules are actually enforced. In this coordination meeting, the two lawyers are aligning their workstreams before the draft is circulated to the partner and then to the client steering committee. The agenda is to confirm what belongs in the 'current regulatory framework' section, which policy document will anchor the 2025 target discussion, whether the enforcement examples are ready for use, and what exactly will be handed off as the source pack. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on section boundaries, annex content, and Thursday handoff responsibilities for the memo and supporting materials.

members.name: Alya Pranowo
members.role: Senior Associate, Environmental and Administrative Law
members.expertise: Environmental compliance, judicial review of regulations, and legal memorandum drafting for public-policy clients
members.background: Alya trained at a top Jakarta firm, clerked briefly at the Supreme Court, and now leads written analysis for complex regulatory matters involving ministries and state coordination bodies.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, defensible memo that the partner can send to the client with minimal revisions, and she is especially concerned about citing only instruments and examples that are unambiguously authoritative and publication-safe.
hidden_assumptions: When a client memo refers to the 'current regulatory framework,' it normally means binding national-level instruments unless local rules are explicitly identified as case studies.
Within this project, 'the action plan' naturally refers to Presidential Regulation No. 83 of 2018 and its formal national action plan annexes, because that is the legally operative anchor.
An 'enforcement example' is ready once there is a publicly citable sanction, judgment, or formal agency action that can support a legal statement without additional fact checking.
A 'source pack' handed to a drafting lead should already be in a form that can be dropped into the Word draft with usable citations, rather than a raw evidence repository.

members.name: Bima Santoso
members.role: Managing Associate, Maritime and Regional Regulation
members.expertise: Regional autonomy, marine governance, port regulation, and Indonesian-language regulatory mapping across central and local agencies
members.background: Bima previously worked with a provincial government legal bureau and has since built a practice around translating on-the-ground regulatory practice into client-facing legal analyses.
members.private_state: He wants the final product to reflect how marine debris regulation actually operates in Indonesia, and he is worried that a purely formal memo will miss the local instruments and informal implementation materials agencies really use.
hidden_assumptions: For marine debris, the 'current regulatory framework' necessarily includes provincial and municipal regulations, as well as ministerial instruments agencies rely on operationally, because those shape real enforcement behavior.

In current inter-agency work, 'the action plan' usually means the National Coordination Team's latest implementation matrix or updated working roadmap, not just the original 2018 presidential instrument.

An 'enforcement example' is not truly ready until the factual sequence, legal basis, and agency role have been checked with local sources so the memo does not overstate scattered enforcement activity.
A 'source pack' means a shared folder of Indonesian originals, unofficial translations, screenshots, and agency-origin materials from which the drafting lawyer will build the formal citations later.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the current regulatory framework
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to cover the 'current regulatory framework' for marine plastic debris in Indonesia.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the main body of the memo will cover binding national instruments such as statutes, government regulations, presidential regulations, and directly relevant ministerial regulations, with local rules used only as optional illustrations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the framework should include not only national instruments but also selected provincial and municipal regulations, plus operational ministry instruments that agencies use in practice, because otherwise the picture is incomplete.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both lawyers are experienced enough that saying 'current regulatory framework' sounds precise and professionally sufficient; neither expects the other to need a discussion about whether local implementation instruments are inside or outside that label.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'action plan' anchors the 2025 target discussion
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the action plan' or the material tied to the 70% reduction by 2025 target.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to Presidential Regulation No. 83 of 2018 and its formal national action plan structure, treating it as the baseline document for legal analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the National Coordination Team's later implementation matrix used in current agency coordination, which updates how the target is tracked and described operationally.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The later working matrix is part of the same policy stream and is commonly discussed as if it were the action plan itself, so shorthand references sound aligned even though they point to different documents.

misalignment_points.topic: When enforcement examples are considered ready
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the 'enforcement examples' will be ready for the memo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'ready' means there is at least one publicly citable example per category with a formal document or official public statement that can be inserted into the draft now.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'ready' means each example has been substantively verified through local contacts so the chronology, responsible agency, and legal basis are reliable enough for a careful annex.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards are professionally reasonable and neither sounds stricter or looser at the surface level; saying something is 'ready' is normal meeting shorthand that rarely gets unpacked unless a deadline slips.

misalignment_points.topic: What the Thursday source-pack handoff will look like
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Bima will send the 'source pack' by Thursday so Alya can finalize citations.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a draftable handoff: a Word or tracked document with authorities already organized for direct citation insertion into her memo sections.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects an evidence handoff: a shared-drive folder containing Indonesian texts, unofficial translations, screenshots, and notes, from which Alya or the drafting team will later build the formal citations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal teams, 'source pack' is a familiar coordination phrase that often goes undefined because everyone assumes a common internal practice, even when different subteams use the term for different deliverable formats.
